title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
publisher: arXiv (UIST '23, ACM); Park, O'Brien, Cai, Morris, Liang, Bernstein (Stanford/Google)

key_points.claim: Agent cognition: LLM-based architecture with memory stream, reflection, and planning yields believable agents in a 25-agent sandbox town (Smallville).
key_points.evidence_quote: an architecture that extends a large language model to store a complete record of the agent’s experiences using natural language, synthesize those memories over time into higher-level reflections, and retrieve them dynamically to plan behavior

key_points.claim: Memory retrieval scores memories by relevance, recency (exponential decay 0.995) and importance (LLM-rated 1–10 poignancy).
key_points.evidence_quote: A memory retrieval model combines relevance, recency, and importance to surface the records needed to inform the agent’s moment-to-moment behavior.

key_points.claim: Agent population and environment: 25 agents, each seeded with a one-paragraph natural-language identity, in a Sims-like world where users can talk to and intervene on agents.
key_points.evidence_quote: A community of 25 unique agents inhabits Smallville.

key_points.claim: Ablation with 100 human evaluators shows every component (observation, planning, reflection) improves believability. Full architecture TrueSkill μ=29.89 versus 21.21 for the prior-work baseline (d=8.16). It also beat human crowdworker-authored behavior (μ=22.95).
key_points.evidence_quote: the full generative agent architecture produced the most believable behavior (𝜇 = 29.89; 𝜎 = 0.72)... 𝑑 = 8.16, or eight standard deviations

key_points.claim: Emergent information diffusion without user intervention over two game days.
key_points.evidence_quote: the number of agents who knew about Sam’s mayoral candidacy increased from one (4%) to eight (32%), and the number of agents who knew about Isabella’s party increased from one (4%) to thirteen (52%)

key_points.claim: Social network / relationship formation: network density rose, with few hallucinated acquaintances.
key_points.evidence_quote: the network density increasing from 0.167 to 0.74. Out of the 453 agent responses regarding their awareness of other agents, 1.3% (n=6) were found to be hallucinated.

key_points.claim: Coordination: a party seeded by a single agent intention led to partial attendance.
key_points.evidence_quote: On Valentine’s Day, five out of the twelve invited agents showed up at Hobbs cafe to join the party.

key_points.claim: Failure modes: agents hallucinate embellishments to their knowledge, though they rarely fabricate it entirely.
key_points.evidence_quote: At times, the agents hallucinated embellishments to their knowledge. It was rare for the agents to completely fabricate their knowledge

key_points.claim: Limitations: high cost, short timescale, and a non-gold-standard human baseline.
key_points.evidence_quote: The present study required substantial time and resources to simulate 25 agents for two days, costing thousands of dollars in token credits and taking multiple days to complete.

key_points.claim: Intended uses: social-science theory testing, populating virtual communities, training for interpersonal situations, prototyping.
key_points.evidence_quote: Such simulations of human behavior could populate virtual spaces and communities with realistic social phenomena

reliability_notes: Full text was read (peer-reviewed UIST '23 paper, arXiv v2). Evaluation is the authors' own, covers only two game days and 25 agents, and uses a crowdworker baseline. Cost and scale limits are acknowledged by the authors.
